title: Alternating with Duke uptown; 'Minnie' becomes a hit
summary: The Cotton Club at 143rd Street and Lenox traded bands between Cab and Duke, and 'Minnie' became a hit on the road.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: after Duke finished that picture and he came back in the Cotton Club -- and they started switching the bands back and forth from Cab to Duke.
I think it was 1929 when we first... '29 or '30. I think I joined the band in '29. So it was around '29 or '30.

So that next summer, when we were on the road, boy, we found out that we had a hit with "Minnie The Moocher." Everybody was asking for "Minnie The Moocher." Then we got how to play it... By that time we memorized it and everything; it was just a matter of playing it. But we got sick of that song, man. [SINGS REFRAIN]
